class.name: HeightmapTerrain3D
class.brief_description: Renders and edits a simple heightmap-based landscape.
class.description: Generates a triangle mesh from a [TerrainHeightmap], including normals, UVs, and vertex colors. The editor provides a brush toolbar for raising, lowering, and coloring the terrain with Undo/Redo. The generated mesh is regenerated when height or color data changes. [b]Note:[/b] The current implementation is intended for small meshes only, as editing any sample rebuilds the entire mesh. Physics collision can be generated and synchronized with height edits when [member auto_collision_enabled] is on; it is off by default. Chunked LOD and world streaming are separate systems.

method.name: get_auto_collision_triangle_count
method.description: Returns the current generated collision triangle count when [member auto_collision_enabled] is active, otherwise 0. The collider is automatically capped at 8192 triangles independently of the visual mesh.

method.name: get_auto_collision_shape
method.description: Returns the current internal concave terrain collision shape, or [code]null[/code] if no shape has been generated. A disabled collider can still retain its last shape to avoid rebuilding when re-enabled.

method.name: build_mesh
method.description: Generates an independent mesh from the current heightmap.

method.name: sample_height_local
method.description: Samples the height at local 3D coordinates, accounting for [member cell_size].

members.member: Opt-in terrain collision through an internal StaticBody3D. The collision surface follows all heightmap geometry edits, while color/material edits do not rebuild an unchanged shape. Live edits are coalesced into a deferred update for physics-server safety.

Minimum heightmap sample stride for the terrain collider (1..16). The engine increases it further if needed to cap the collider at 8192 triangles. The visual mesh retains the full original sampling resolution.
Distance in local units between adjacent samples.
Heightmap resource from which the mesh is generated.
Optional material assigned to the generated surface. By default, a standard material displays the painted vertex colors.
